title: The popular version. A cow started the fire.
description:
A cow started the fire. It began on the evening of 8 October 1871 in the O'Leary family barn on DeKoven Street. Smithsonian reports the Chicago Evening Journal implicated Catherine O'Leary before the fire died out.

Nobody could say what started it. The 1871 inquiry reported, in Smithsonian and Mental Floss, that we are unable to determine the cause.

A reporter made up the cow. Wikipedia, Ripley's and Mental Floss all report that Michael Ahern admitted he fabricated the story. Mental Floss says he and two colleagues invented it to add colour.

About 300 people died and around 100,000 were left homeless, according to Smithsonian and Mental Floss. The blame landed on one woman.

She was an easy scapegoat. Smithsonian cites ethnic stereotypes and nativist fears. Ripley's names anti Irish and anti Catholic sentiment.

Formally exonerated Catherine O'Leary of responsibility for the fire. She had died on 3 July 1895.

The city took 126 years to clear her name.

Sources:
- https://www.smithsonianmag.com/history/what-or-who-caused-the-great-chicago-fire-61481977/: read in full. Established that the fire began on Sunday 8 October 1871 in the barn on DeKoven Street, that the Chicago Evening Journal implicated Catherine O'Leary before the fire died out, about 300 lives lost and 100,000 left homeless, the inquiry conclusion we are unable to determine, nativist fears and ethnic stereotypes, and the 1997 City Council resolution exonerating Catherine and her cow.
- https://www.mentalfloss.com/article/12864/did-cow-really-cause-great-chicago-fire: read in full. Established the around 9pm start on 8 October 1871, about 300 deaths and 100,000 homeless, that the reporter and two colleagues made up the cow story to add colour, and the inquiry conclusion we are unable to determine.
- https://www.ripleys.com/stories/olearys-chicago-fire-cow: read in full. Established that Michael Ahern retracted his statements and said he made it up, the anti Irish, anti Catholic and anti immigrant sentiment, and the 1997 exoneration.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine_O%27Leary: read in full. Established that the fire began in the O'Leary family barn on the evening of 8 October 1871, that Ahern admitted he fabricated the story, that anti Irish sentiment contributed to the family being scapegoats, that the council formally exonerated her, and that she died on 3 July 1895.
